threads.body: `fieldName` comes from the new public API and is copied verbatim into generated class, field, and method names. An allowed value such as `"request.id"` therefore creates an injected field/getter containing `.`, which is forbidden in JVM unqualified names; names containing the `$` delimiter can also make distinct mapping tuples resolve to the same generated class name. Please either validate a clearly documented restricted alphabet or use a lossless, collision-free encoding before constructing generated names.

The new public behavior has no end-to-end coverage: the added tests verify mapping collection and generated strings, while the existing `testing-common/integration-tests` virtual-field test exercises only the two-argument API. Please extend that integration instrumentation to create two differently named fields with the same owner/value types and verify that their values remain independent through Muzzle generation, field injection, and runtime lookup.

@trask do you have any suggestions on what the argument order should be?

replies.body:
I guess I like

> Class<T> type, Class<F> fieldType, String fieldName

as that matches source declaration order and matches the existing overload

another good option is

> Class<T> type, String fieldName, Class<F> fieldType

which matches `MethodHandles.Lookup.findGetter(Class, String, Class)`

especially if we are thinking to deprecate the original method and require field name
